svg.text: Sketches by the brand-research agent to show structure, not final artwork. Type shown in generic system faces;
the shipped identity should use a face that can be justified from Nigerian print, sleeve and poster history (see §10, R2).
D1 — "Fixed invariant, variable ordering" · one wordmark, a registered set of states [RECOMMENDED]
Precedent: Tate (Wolff Olins 2000 — standard / blurred / faded / halftone). Principle source: Uli practice, where motifs stay consistent and "the ordering of the design elements" is the creative act.
D2 — "Masthead, not logo" · zero symbol, publication register
Precedent: The Gentlewoman, Fantastic Man, The Republic (wordmark shipped as SVG), n+1, Nka. The New Yorker has held one masthead for a century.

g.text: a digital museum of Nigeria's creative history

svg.text: Precedent: MoMA (Chermayeff 1964, Franklin Gothic No. 2 — unchanged for 60 years), Whitney (Experimental Jetset 2013), Library of Congress and National Gallery of Art (Pentagram).
Precedent: Cooper Hewitt (Opara / Pentagram 2014 — identity issued with the museum's wordmark and site redesign).
Deliberately absent from every direction above: a globe, a continent outline, an invented tribal device, a kente-stripe block, a green-white-green divider, and a standalone pictorial symbol.
Those are the archetypes catalogued in ANTI-PATTERN-SCHEMATICS.svg and excluded by SKU §6.
Rule of thumb for whichever direction is chosen: the wordmark must remain legible and self-identical at 16px, at billboard scale, in one colour, and as a solid block — then earn its states.
